chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who leads the people in prayer while you are not pleased with him, in a prayer in which the recitation is audible.
So he said: When you hear the Book of Allah being recited, then listen silently to it.

I said: But he testifies against me with shirk. He said: If he disobeys Allah, then obey Allah. I repeated the matter to him, but he refused to grant me a concession. He said: So I said to him: Shall I then pray in my house and then go out to him? He said: That is up to you.

So the correct understanding regarding these two reports is the state of taqiyyah and fear, because when the situation is like that, it is permissible for a person to recite to himself inwardly and not raise his voice; this indicates that.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection in dangerous circumstances
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: fear that creates a legally relevant circumstance
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an being recited
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads the people in prayer as Imam

ai.seo_question: Can one recite in prayer behind an Imam who is not fit to be followed in audible salat?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying behind one who is not fit to be followed in an audible salat. It instructs silence when the Book of Allah is recited, while also indicating, in a situation of taqiyyah and fear, that one may recite inwardly without raising the voice. The report is used in the context of legal discussion on recitation behind an unsuitable prayer leader.
